result.reasoning:
REFUTED on two independent grounds, the first verified numerically.

(1) The load-bearing claim is false. The finding's core assertion is that the quantile estimator is "one of several standard conventions a reader cannot recover from the text alone". The text does name it. The sibling docstring at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:304-309 states the tail is the "Same tail as ``cross_quantile_q25``" -- an operator that exists in this engine -- and the module header at ops_ext.py:11 states "Conventions (the same as AlphaCube's kernels)". That named operator is literally `torch.nanquantile(w, q, dim=-1)` at /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/operators/dt_cross.py:212-214. I re-implemented the docstring SENTENCE literally, taking "the 75% quantile of the last d days" to be that named operator (never touching _tail_mean), and it reproduces both kernels BIT-FOR-BIT: max |diff| = 0.000e+00 with identical NaN masks, across the reporter's own [1,2,3,4] window, 400x60 panels at d=4/5/30/60, 30% and 60% NaN (so n down to the n>=2 guard), heavy-tailed Amt-like data, and all-integer data where every window is ties. Following the docstring's own cross-reference lands on exactly the implemented numbers -- the estimator is pinned by the text, uniquely, inside this repo.

(2) The rule the finding invokes does not say what it needs it to say. ops_ext.py:9 reads "The docstring of each kernel is its definition.  Read that, not the name." -- the second sentence makes it a "do not infer semantics from the name" rule. The governing doc spells the same rule out as docstring AND code (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md:7: "每个算子的定义以 ops_ext.py 里的 docstring 和代码为准"). Nothing holds the docstring to be a standalone estimator-level spec. new_operators.md:30 also documents q25/q75 as ONE row ("cross_tail_mean_q25(x, d) / …_q75"), so isolating q75's docstring from its sibling's cross-reference contradicts the report's own framing ("both delegate to the same _tail_mean quantile call").

(3) No number or conclusion can move, so it fails the review bar regardless. The reporter concedes "Not a bug in the current code". Grep over studies/, lab/, partura/, research/ finds no second implementation -- _tail_mean (ops_ext.py:293) is the only one, so no docstring misreading is ever evaluated. At the only window lengths the operator is actually used with (d=30 and d=60, in research/alpha_distillation/B01_upgrades_and_fusion.md:88 and :94) the alternative "lower" reading has median cross-sectional rank correlation 0.9949 (d=30) and 0.9980 (d=60) against the implemented one; since the selection口径 reads only the cross-sectional ORDER (top-10% equal-weight long book), neither reading could flip a selection verdict. The divergence the reporter exhibits (mean |diff| 0.36, rank-corr 0.90) needs d=4, a window no expression uses. For completeness, partura/steer.py:168 already groups cross_tail_mean_q25/q75 with cross_quantile_q25/q75 in the same SIGN_KEEPING_OPS family, treating them as one convention.

(4) Reproduction outcome: I did trigger the described behaviour -- cross_tail_mean_q75 on one stock with window [1,2,3,4] returns exactly 4.0 -- but that output is CORRECT under the convention the text names, so per the brief ("触发了但结果其实是对的,就判 refuted=true") confirmed_by_reproduction stays false. This is a documentation-precision remark in the class the review mandate excludes (风格/命名/注释不报).
